learning_outcomes.text: Students learn to model and solve problems using the methods of logic.
Students learn to construct formal proofs and understand their relationship to informal ones.
Students acquire the fundamentals of theoretical concepts (model, semantics, soundness, completeness), enabling them to study more advanced logical methods with applications in computer science.

syllabus_topics: Tarski’s semantics and an introduction to classical model theory
Introduction to proof theory, logical calculus (e.g., tableaux), soundness and completeness
Overview of logic and inference applications, e.g., in databases, knowledge representations, artificial intelligence

assessment_methods.method: Final written exam (problem solving and theory)

assessment_rules:
Admission to the final exam requires at least 60% in continuous assessment. The final exam consists of two parts (problem solving and theory), with at least 60% required in each part. The overall assessment is based on a 60/40 proportion for continuous assessment and final exam respectively. Grading scale: A 

92%, B 

84%, C 

76%, D 

68%, E 

60%.
